north.title: North Mississippi
north.heading: Ecology of North Mississippi
north.info: North Mississippi has many native species that are more accustomed to temperate broadleaf and mixed forests. This isn't to say that there aren't any wetland dwelling species native to the northern regions, however. This is still Mississippi we're talking about. Northern Mississippi is still filled with wetlands and marshes, however, they are much more to the west in the Delta region.

aa.title: American Alligator
aa.sub: The American Alligator is a ferocious carnivore that resides in the wetlands of Northern Mississippi.
aa.f1: Also known as the Mississippi alligator
aa.f2: Its lifespan can be up to 40 years in the wild.
aa.f3: Its weight can be upwards of 450 lbs, with some growing even larger.
aa.f4: The American Alligator is an apex predator in its respective habitat, having no other animal that preys on it.
aa.f5: They are most likely identified from their wetland habitats, their broad and rounded U-shaped snout, and their increased tooth visibility.

wtd.title: White-tailed Deer
wtd.sub: A herbivore that serves a key prey species for many of the ecosystems that it inhabits.
wtd.f1: They inhabit much of the mixed forests of northern Mississippi.
wtd.f2: Their lifespan can range up to 4.5 years.
wtd.f3: They can grow to be 160 lbs.
wtd.f4: Their top speed is a whopping 30 miles per hour.
wtd.f5: They have a very notable sexual dimorphism like most deer, as males (bucks) have antlers that they shed while females (does) do not.

wbc.title: Wooly Bear Caterpillar
wbc.sub: This little guy is an herbivore that sports fuzzy black and red stripes that attempt to deceive predators into thinking they are poisonous.
wbc.f1: Also known as a wooly worm.
wbc.f2: They eventually pupate into the Isabella tiger moth, which is much less colorful than their larval stage.
wbc.f4: Their lifespan ranges to about 1 year.
wbc.f5: They generally weigh less than a gram, clocking in at about 0.68 g.

ms.title: Moccasin Snake
ms.sub: These slithering carnivores have a notable pale mouth interior that gives them their common name.
ms.f1: Also known as a cottonmouth or water moccasin.
ms.f2: Their lifespan can range up to 12 years.
ms.f3: They can grow up to 2 lbs and 4 feet in length.

south.title: South Mississippi
south.heading: Ecology of South Mississippi
south.info: South Mississippi is home to various different biomes that range from coastal beaches to mixed forests and pinelands. The fauna that inhabit these ecosystems are diverse and interesting organisms that are uniquely specialized to fill their niche.

rs.title: Roseate Spoonbill
rs.sub: These coastal piscivores eat fish, crabs, and other small coastal prey animals.
rs.f1: They are wading birds, meaning they use their long legs to wade into the surf and use their specialized beak to search for food.
rs.f2: Their lifespan can range up to 10 years.
rs.f3: They can grow up to 1.8 lbs with a wingspan of 47 to 53 inches.
rs.f4: They have a notable bright pink body that they get their name from.

fhc.title: Flathead Catfish
fhc.sub: These Mississippi staples are piscivores, meaning they eat mainly fish and other seafood.
fhc.f1: Also known as a Shovelnose Cat.
fhc.f2: Their lifespans can range up to 15 years.
fhc.f3: They can weigh up to 57 lbs and grow up to 61 inches in length (Record Catch).
fhc.f4: They have been introduced to many other regions in the U.S., but they are native to the Gulf Coast region.

rbw.title: Red-Bellied Woodpecker
rbw.sub: They are omnivorous birds native to much of southern Mississippi, as well as much of the southeast U.S.
rbw.f1: Their lifespans can range up to 4 years.
rbw.f2: They can grow up to 0.09 lbs.
rbw.f3: Despite their name, the most notable feature on the Red-Bellied Woodpecker is their bright red plum on their crown and back of neck. The red on their chest is very subtle in comparison.

bs.title: Bonnethead Shark
bs.sub: These omnivorous cartilaginous fish inhabit much of the Gulf Coast region of southern Mississippi.
bs.f1: Their lifespans can range up to 9 years
bs.f2: They can grow up to 10 lbs and 59 inches in length.
bs.f3: They are in the hammerhead family of sharks, of which it is the smallest species.
bs.f4: They are often found in bays or estuaries.
